## CORRECTION — the previous comment's commit `ce3b62144aeb` would have FAILED CI

**Superseded by `e2ca5803298bedf81c3c2ccca47e982635231203`.** Disregard the SHA in the
"Phase 2 (Repair) complete" comment above; everything else in it stands.

### The defect I shipped, and how I nearly missed it

`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` was at **exactly 800 LOC** on `origin/main` — already at
the locked hard cap in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`. The 8-line `# tickets-boundary-ok:`
sanction block took it to **804**, breaching a cap the repo documents as ABSOLUTE with no
allowlist and no exemptions.

**`make lint` does not catch this.** The module-size gate is a step in
`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, not a Makefile target, so my green local verification —
`make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0, 4276 tests — was all consistent with a commit CI
would have rejected. That is the precise gap: a locally-green tree is not a CI-green tree when
the gate lives only in the workflow.

**I made it worse before I made it better.** The implementing subagent had already spotted this
and pushed a 4-line reflow that restored 800. I saw an uncommitted post-commit edit, judged it
on its *diff content* (a comment rewording) rather than its *purpose* (the line count), called
it "unverified drift", and reverted it — reintroducing the breach. The subagent's report then
independently flagged the same 804 figure, which is what prompted me to actually measure. Two
separate signals pointed at this before I checked; the lesson is that "cosmetic-looking diff in
a file already at a hard limit" is never safely cosmetic.

### Fix and verification

Re-applied the 4-line form of the sanction — meaning and the mandatory reason preserved,
marker still adjacent to `_TRACKER_DIRNAME` as the boundary gate requires — and amended.

    repo_snapshot.py: 804 -> 800

Verified with **CI's exact command**, not an approximation of it:

    $ LIMIT=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < .github/module-size-limit.txt)
    $ find src/rebar -name '*.py' | grep -v __pycache__ | xargs wc -l \
        | awk -v lim="$LIMIT" '$2 != "total" && $1 > lim { print $1 " " $2 }'
    (no output)
    Module-size gate: OK — no src/rebar file exceeds the 800-LOC hard cap

    $ pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py     -> 4 passed
    $ python scripts/check_tickets_boundary.py           -> exit 0
    $ pytest <held-out oracle> <guard> <module-size>     -> 25 passed
    $ make lint                                          -> exit 0
    $ make typecheck                                     -> Success: 678 source files
    $ verify-commit-ticket --rev e2ca5803298b            -> OK - resolved 0514-92e0-e6c4-4304

`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` mirrors the CI gate and **was never in my earlier test
selection** (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` + `tests/interfaces/facades`), which is the mechanical
reason the 4276-test run stayed green. The full `tests/unit` tier is running now; I will record
its result.

Three files now sit at exactly 800 (`reconcile.py`, `reconcile_helpers.py`, `repo_snapshot.py`),
so **any future comment added to them breaches the cap.** That is a real maintenance edge left
for the next contributor, and it is a consequence of this change budgeting them to the line.

### Residual risk added to the list

- **Local gates are not the full CI gate set.** `make lint` omits the module-size gate. Anyone
  verifying a change locally in this repo should also run the CI awk command above, or at least
  `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`.
- **Three files at exactly 800.** Splitting one of them along an existing call-graph seam would
  buy back the headroom this change consumed. Not done here — it is out of scope for a bug fix
  and would need its own plan review.
